requirements.text: The user must undo and redo its last thousand actions.
The product must count and display the time that the user uses to play.
The product must count and display the number of the user'saction.
The product must record the score (time and number of counts) of a play associated with the name of a user.
The product must display a window with all the player'sscores.
The main window shall provide the following parts : A board, see chapter 3.2.1.1. a menu bar, see chapter 3.2.5.
The user can cancel a movement.
The user can redo a movement that has been canceled.
The following statistics are recorded during the game : number of block movements since the start. time since the start.
The user could erase all the statistics.
The software must be portable to the Windows OS.
The application must validate the integrity and structure of any saved game file before loading it, ensuring it conforms to the expected schema and contains no executable code or malformed data.
The statistics file must be stored in a secure, user-specific directory with restricted write permissions to prevent unauthorized tampering or deletion by other users on the same machine.
The application must restrict file operations to a designated application-specific directory and prevent directory traversal by validating file paths.
The system shall implement atomic write operations for save files and statistics to ensure data integrity in the event of application crashes or disk failures.
The application shall limit the undo/redo history buffer to a maximum of 1000 actions to maintain a predictable memory footprint.
The system shall validate the schema of save files upon opening and reject files that do not conform to the expected version format to prevent undefined behavior.
The application shall perform undo/redo operations in under 100ms and maintain the 1000-action history within a memory limit of 50MB.
All UI interactions, including block movement and menu navigation, shall have a response latency of less than 50ms.
The statistics file shall be capped at a fixed size (e.g., 10 entries) and operations must complete within 200ms to prevent UI blocking.
